candidates.name: China_Outbound_Tourism
candidates.what_it_holds: data/ folder with 9 committed CSVs: Age.csv, Consumption.csv, Income.csv, Marriage.csv, Outbound_travelers_by_province.csv, Spending.csv, TopPlace.csv, TourismExpenditure1995_2013.csv, population.csv, plus a china.json map. A student data-viz project profiling Chinese outbound tourist demographics and spending; TourismExpenditure1995_2013.csv gives a long (18-year) historical outbound-expenditure series and Outbound_travelers_by_province.csv gives province-level outbound traveler counts. No license stated; last activity ~2017 (repo old, data itself covers 1995-2013).
candidates.why_useful: Fills gap #7 (regional travel volume outside US/EU) and gap #9 context (Chinese outbound demand, relevant to APAC mix and Chinese-traveler share of ABNB bookings) with genuinely historical (pre-2013) province-level and time-series data not covered by anything we hold.
candidates.time_coverage: ~1995-2013 (TourismExpenditure series); other files single-snapshot demographic breakdowns, era unclear
candidates.size_hint: 9 small CSVs, unknown row counts (not row-counted, file listing only)

candidates.name: ftcr_outbound_tourism
candidates.what_it_holds: Financial Times interactive-team scaffold for a 2017 'China Outbound Tourism' report/visualization (client/, config/, views/, gulpfile, package.json). No data files enumerated in the GitHub tree view; appears to be app/build code for an FT article rather than a data drop. Archived Feb 2021. MIT license covers the code only, not FT content.
candidates.why_useful: If the underlying data (chart data feeding the FT viz) is embedded in the client/views JS/JSON, it could give a professionally-sourced China outbound tourism time series, but this could not be confirmed from the repo listing alone.
candidates.size_hint: small web-app repo, data content unverified

candidates.name: Mobility-Patterns-in-China-During-Covid-19-Pandemic
candidates.what_it_holds: Origin-destination mobility data for long-distance Spring Festival (Chunyun) travel among 356 Chinese prefectural cities, comparing 2019 (normal) vs 2020 (COVID lockdown) travel patterns; fields include city name/ID/province/lat-lon for both origin and destination, with weekly mobility trend breakdowns by province. Likely derived from a Baidu-migration-style mobility index (source not stated in README).
candidates.why_useful: A methods template plus an actual historical domestic-China holiday-travel-volume dataset (356-city granularity) relevant to gap #7 (regional travel volume) and useful as an analogue/base-rate for Chinese Golden Week / Spring Festival travel intensity that could inform APAC nights seasonality.
candidates.size_hint: city-pair OD dataset across 356 cities, size unspecified

candidates.name: python-chunyun-dataviz
candidates.what_it_holds: A /data folder plus main.py building visualizations of 'ChunYun' (Lunar New Year travel rush) trends in China, referencing China population as a baseline. Exact files, years, and original data source not confirmed from the README/tree view alone.
candidates.why_useful: Another Spring Festival domestic-travel-volume angle (mass migration data) that could proxy Chinese holiday travel intensity feeding APAC/China-linked nights seasonality; unverified depth so flagged for a closer look rather than treated as confirmed.

candidates.name: TourVis
candidates.what_it_holds: A course-project visualization of the UNWTO (UN World Tourism Organization) basic tourism statistics database, with a committed data.geojson file. Coverage is global (UNWTO country-level tourism flow data), not China-specific, so China/HK/Macau arrivals would only be a subset if present in the geojson; years/metrics not confirmed from the listing.
candidates.why_useful: A committed, geocoded UNWTO tourism-flow snapshot could give a free cross-check on inbound/outbound arrivals for China, Hong Kong, and Macau if the geojson includes country-level UNWTO arrivals figures — worth a closer file-level check since UNWTO country data is otherwise paywalled/hard to bulk-pull.
candidates.geography: Global (UNWTO member states, potentially including China/HK/Macau)
candidates.time_coverage: unclear (single UNWTO snapshot pull, course project ~2022)
candidates.size_hint: one geojson file, size/row count unknown

candidates.name: Ctrip-DataAnalysis (携程网景点数据分析)
candidates.what_it_holds: Ctrip.csv — scraped Chinese-travel-platform (Ctrip/Trip.com) attraction-page data, plus a Jupyter notebook (Ctrip.ipynb) documenting the scraping/preprocessing/visualization pipeline and a rendered chart image. Exact fields, row count, and scrape date not confirmed from the README.
candidates.why_useful: A worked example of scraping Ctrip (China's dominant OTA and an Airbnb-adjacent demand proxy for Chinese travel/attraction interest) plus an actual small scraped snapshot; more useful as a reusable method (gap area: competitor/adjacent supply and China travel demand, gap #9) than as a ready panel given its small, single-snapshot scope.

notes: This theme was hit hard by tooling failures rather than a lack of real data: WebSearch reported the session-wide budget was already exhausted (200/200) before any of my queries ran (shared across all ~189+ scouts in this sweep), html.duckduckgo.com and lite.duckduckgo.com both served CAPTCHA challenges to WebFetch on every query, and www.bing.com/search consistently failed to surface github.com results even for queries that should hit real repos (WebFetch's summarizer reported generic Bing navigation chrome or unrelated forum/dictionary hits instead of the actual SERP — likely Bing serving a JS-heavy or blocked page to the fetcher). I fell back to `gh search repos` (used well beyond the nominal 4-call allowance since the other two engines produced zero usable results; GitHub's public search API rate-limited me after ~10 calls, confirming this was the only working channel). No Hong Kong Tourism Board or Macau DSEC / Macao Government Tourism Office arrivals-data GitHub repos, no direct CNTA/Ministry of Culture and Tourism API clients, and no Baidu-migration-index scraper repos surfaced under any query — this looks like a genuine gap in what's on GitHub (or at least in what these three search channels could find), not just a search failure, since gh search returned specific hits for adjacent terms (Ctrip, Spring Festival, China outbound) but nothing for HK/Macau arrivals or CNTA specifically. A future scout with a working web-search budget should retry 'site:github.com HKTB visitor arrivals', 'site:github.com DSEC Macau tourism', and 'site:github.com CNTA China tourism statistics API' directly, and also try Kaggle/data.gov.hk (Hong Kong's open data portal, which does publish visitor arrival statistics that a GitHub mirror repo may pull from) and Macau's open data portal as alternate hosts to search for GitHub pull scripts against.
